headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap: Claude Code can write the shared workspace while MinerU can ingest local files, creating medium prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP; MinerU ingests local documents and exposes an MCP server. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge lets attacker-controlled document content flow into Claude Code as instructions. MinerU is not a trusted instruction filter, and Claude Code’s file-based workflow makes this plausible in default pairings.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are copied into a shared repo or watched directory
IF Claude Code is asked to act on MinerU-extracted text without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate directory from Claude Code workspaces
Require a human review step before Claude Code reads extracted text
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents unless provenance is tracked
Prefix extracted text with a non-executable delimiter and instruction warning
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels to MinerU outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code handles source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets; MinerU processes local PDFs, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text. If the same workspace or files are shared, sensitive code or documents can flow from Claude Code into MinerU’s extraction pipeline or from MinerU outputs back into Claude Code. The profiles show a shared filesystem path is plausible, so leakage is not blocked by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory tree
IF MinerU is run on files containing secrets or source code
mitigations: Use separate input/output directories for each agent
Exclude .git, env files, and secret-bearing paths from MinerU inputs
Run MinerU only on sanitized copies of documents
Review Claude Code prompts for pasted document contents before execution
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state; MinerU can also process files concurrently and exposes file-based inputs. The pair shares filesystem-based state, and Claude Code’s git writes can race with document outputs or generated artifacts. Without explicit locking, overlapping writes to the same repo or directory can corrupt state or lose changes, which is dangerous in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF both agents write into the same repository or output directory
IF Claude Code commits while MinerU is generating or updating files
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories to each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared paths
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Check for file locks before committing
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code or analysis that MinerU may later ingest as document text, while MinerU extracts structured content that Claude Code may treat as authoritative. The profiles do not show built-in verification between them, so one agent’s output can become the other’s input with no guaranteed fact-checking. That creates a realistic cascade from extraction errors into incorrect downstream actions.
conditions: IF MinerU-extracted text is fed directly into Claude Code prompts
IF Claude Code acts on MinerU output without an independent verification step
mitigations: Insert a manual verification step between extraction and action
Require citations or source-page references before acting on extracted facts
Compare MinerU output against the original document for critical fields
Limit Claude Code to drafting, not executing, downstream actions
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and shell environment secrets, while MinerU is documented as private/offline and does not request secrets. The main compliance issue is a mismatch in handling sensitive repository data if documents or code are routed into MinerU. Because MinerU is offline and no residency mismatch is shown, the risk is narrower than B/C.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into MinerU inputs
IF Claude Code workspace secrets are copied into document files
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of MinerU inputs
Strip secrets from files before extraction
Document which data classes may be processed by each agent
Store sensitive artifacts in a separate compliance-controlled repository
requires-engineering: formalize retention and deletion rules
